title: Backfill 90 days of unit economics data + validate vs Finance tie-out; document known gaps
creator: Logan Wright
description:
Goal
Backfill 90 days of historical partitions for the unit economics dataset(s) used by the internal dashboard, validate totals vs Finance expectations (billing/metering tie-out), and publish a short “known gaps/limitations” note so Product/Finance know what not to over-interpret.

Context
The unit economics dashboard is intended to be the source of truth for blended cost ($/1M output tokens) with drilldowns by model/region/tier. For launch we need enough historical depth for trendlines and mix-shift comparisons. Finance also needs a tie-out view that reconciles dashboard totals to billing/metering within an agreed tolerance.

Scope
- Backfill 90 days of: daily blended $/1M output tokens aggregates at the agreed grain (day x model_variant x region x tier) + supporting numerator/denominator fields.
- Ensure tier mapping is historically correct for the entire backfill range (depends on ENG-2911).
- Run reconciliation job for the same 90-day range and capture variance notes (depends on ENG-2914).
- Document known gaps (data availability, tag introduction dates, late-arriving event behavior, region mapping changes) in a short internal note and link from the ticket.

Out of scope
- Backfilling any pre-90-day history.
- Changing canonical metric definitions (see ADR-0142).
- Building new dashboard UI elements (ENG-2916).

Acceptance criteria
1) Data availability
- Daily partitions exist for the last 90 days in the production analytics table(s) used by the dashboard.
- All required dimensions are populated per the data contract (model, region, tier; null rate < 0.1% for required dims, excluding explicitly documented exceptions).

2) Reconciliation / tie-out
- Overall (all regions/all tiers) blended cost numerator and output token denominator reconcile to billing/metering within tolerance agreed with FP&A for the backfill period.
- Reconciliation also computed by region and by tier; any slices outside tolerance are annotated with root cause hypothesis and whether it is expected/acceptable.
- Share tie-out summary with Rishi Malhotra (FP&A) + Laura Bennett (CFO) for sign-off.

3) Known gaps documented
- A single doc (Confluence page or Drive note) linked here that lists:
  - known missing fields by time range (e.g., tags introduced mid-window)
  - limitations of late-event handling/backfill cutoffs
  - any region/tier mapping changes that affect historical comparability
  - recommended “do not use” interpretations (e.g., slice X before date Y)

Implementation plan
- Pre-flight
  - Confirm tier mapping backfill plan is complete (ENG-2911).
  - Confirm reconciliation job + alerting is deployed (ENG-2914) and can run ad hoc for historical partitions.
  - Validate current partition strategy and backfill tooling supports dry-run + idempotent re-runs (see runbook: unit-econ-pipeline-backfill-runbook).

- Backfill execution
  - Run backfill in “dry-run” mode for 3 days to validate:
    - schema matches expected
    - partition overwrite behavior is correct
    - join cardinality is stable
  - Run full 90-day backfill in batches (e.g., 7-day windows) to limit blast radius.
  - After each batch: run basic data quality checks (row counts, nulls, negative/zero tokens where invalid, top-k dimension distributions).

- Tie-out / reconciliation
  - Run reconciliation job for the full 90-day range.
  - Produce a small summary table:
    - variance % overall
    - variance % by region
    - variance % by tier
    - top 5 worst slices + notes
  - If variance spikes are driven by late-arriving metering events, confirm the agreed cutoff rule (e.g., exclude T-1 or T-2 day partitions from “official” reporting) and document.

- Documentation
  - Write “Known gaps and interpretation guidance (90-day backfill)” note.
  - Include: exact backfill window, runtime commit/tag used, any manual interventions, and links to reconciliation output.

Open questions
- Confirm final reconciliation tolerance with FP&A for slice-level views (overall vs per-region/per-tier).
- Confirm whether Finance wants credits/discounts excluded from this backfill validation run (metric is “blended cost” per ADR, but tie-out sometimes prefers pre-credit COGS view).

Links
- Epic: PM-482
- Related eng work: ENG-2910 (dataset), ENG-2911 (tier mapping), ENG-2914 (reconciliation job), ENG-2917 (data quality monitoring)
- PRs: PR-11842 (aggregation job), PR-11871 (reconciliation), PR-11914 (backfill tooling)
- Support reference: SUP-8841 (historical mismatch due to region mapping + late metering events)

Deliverables
- 90-day backfill complete in production tables
- Reconciliation summary shared with Finance + sign-off recorded in ticket comments
- Known gaps doc linked here
comments: 2025-02-06 (Logan Wright): Creating this as the “last mile” for launch readiness. Finance asked for 90 days minimum so they can compare to monthly COGS and see mix shifts. Mei to own execution; Cole (billing recon) can help if we hit metering edge cases.

2025-02-08 (Mei Lin): Pre-flight: tier mapping table backfill from ENG-2911 is ready in staging; waiting on prod rollout. I ran a 3-day dry-run backfill (T-10..T-8) in staging and validated schema + partition overwrite behavior. No cardinality explosions observed; row counts stable vs expected model/region distributions.

2025-02-12 (Mei Lin): Ran first batch backfill in prod for 2024-11-15..2024-11-30. Data quality checks passed (required dims null <0.05%). Noted that quantization_profile is NULL for ~98% rows in this time range (expected; tags were introduced later). Will document as known gap.

2025-02-14 (Mei Lin): Completed full 90-day backfill in prod (2024-11-22..2025-02-19). Reconciliation job run for the full window: overall variance at +0.38% vs billing/metering totals. Biggest outlier slice: eu-west/self_serve on 2025-01-03 (+2.4%) likely due to late metering events + region mapping update; investigating with Cole Summers.

2025-02-17 (Cole Summers): Looked at eu-west 2025-01-03 variance. Billing side shows a late metering batch landed on 2025-01-05 but attributed to service day 2025-01-03. Our pipeline cutoff for “official” daily partitions currently treats T-1 as final; for backfill we didn’t reprocess after 48h. Suggest documenting that daily numbers can drift for ~72h and Finance reporting should use T-3 as stable. This matches the discussion in #eng-platform last week.

2025-02-18 (Mei Lin): Re-ran affected partitions (2025-01-01..2025-01-07) with late-event window extended; eu-west/self_serve variance improved to +0.9%. Overall variance now +0.31%. Updating known gaps doc to recommend T-3 cutoff for weekly review metrics.

2025-02-20 (Mei Lin): Drafted “Known gaps and interpretation guidance (90-day backfill)” and shared with Rishi for review. Remaining: FP&A sign-off on tolerance + confirmation we’re good with slice-level variances up to ~1% when late events are involved. Marking In Review pending Finance sign-off.
